title: Multimode Parametric Amplifier for K-Band Quantum Measurements
abstract: We demonstrate K-band nondegenerate three-wave-mixing amplification in a multimode resonator comprising an array of 500 SNAILs. Pairing K-band signal modes with lower-frequency internal idler modes enables 20 dB of gain continuously from 19.6 to 25.6 GHz with pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz. At 20 dB gain, the 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 2.6 to 11.7 MHz, and the input-referred 1-dB compression power reaches -100.9 dBm. In the 20-22 GHz band, the average added noise is 0.73 quanta. A two-mode nondegenerate parametric amplification model describes the measured gain response and gain-bandwidth behavior, while a multimode Kerr model captures the overall compression scale. Our amplifier provides a practical solution for implementing a state-of-the-art readout of superconducting qubits in the K-band.
summary: This paper reports on a high-performance, multimode parametric amplifier designed for reading out superconducting qubits in the K-band. By utilizing nondegenerate three-wave-mixing in an array of SNAILs, the authors achieved 20 dB of gain with low added noise. The combination of experimental validation and advanced theoretical modeling provides a practical quantum measurement tool.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a practical, state-of-the-art readout amplifier for superconducting qubits operating in the K-band (19.6–25.6 GHz).
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated high-gain (20 dB), low-added-noise (0.73 quanta), and broadband parametric amplification in the K-band using a multimode resonator.
method: The work combines experimental measurements of gain and noise with theoretical modeling using both a two-mode Nondegenerate Parametric Amplifier (NDPA) model and a multimode Kerr model.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a multimode resonator built from an array of 500 Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive Elements (SNAILs). The amplification relies on nondegenerate three-wave-mixing ($\omega_p \simeq \omega_s + \omega_i$).
key_observables: Gain (20 dB), 3-dB bandwidth (2.6 to 11.7 MHz), input-referred 1-dB compression power (-100.9 dBm), and average added noise (0.73 quanta).
important_parameters: K-band frequencies (19.6–25.6 GHz), pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz, and the quantum limit for added noise (1/2 quantum).
main_assumptions: The Kerr-limited model employs the stiff-pump approximation, and the perturbative calculation for dispersive shifts is limited to self- and two-mode virtual processes.
figures_summary: Figures compare measured gain traces to the two-mode NDPA fit, show the input-referred 1-dB compression power versus signal frequency compared to Kerr-limited calculations, and characterize added noise versus inverse gain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system and the need for nondegenerate mixing, to detailing the Hamiltonian and modeling approach (NDPA and Kerr models), and finally presenting the quantitative measurements of gain, bandwidth, and noise performance.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the quantum measurement interface for superconducting qubits, which is a core topic in quantum computing. The detailed modeling of nonlinear effects and noise characterization is highly relevant to open quantum systems theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Device concept and multimode spectrum of the distributed SNAIL parametric amplifier (SPA). (a) Frequency-domain comparison between degenerate three-wave mixing, ωp ≃2ωs, and the nondegenerate process used here, ωp ≃ωs + ωi with ωi < ωs. (b) Circuit repre- sentation of the short–open nonlinear resonator containing 500 SNAIL cells. (c) Flux-dependent spectroscopy of modes 6–8 (markers) and simultaneous fit to the linear multimode model (curves). (d) Calculated zero-flux mode spectrum and independently extracted mode-frequency anchors used in the fit.

FIG. 2. Nondegenerate gain and bandwidth. The upper bars indicate the frequency coverage of the 7–3 and 8–2 signal–idler combinations. (a),(b) Measured gain traces for the 7–3 and 8–2 combinations; each inset compares a measured trace with the corresponding two-mode NDPA fit. (c) Measured 3-dB bandwidth normalized to 20-dB peak gain, BW20dB = BWpGpeak/10, and the corrected harmonic-mean linewidth calculated from the signal and idler linewidths using the full pump-off-normalized model.

FIG. 3. Input-referred 1-dB compression power versus signal fre- quency for the 7–3 and 8–2 signal–idler combinations. Markers show measurements referred to the SPA input plane. Solid curves show the Kerr-limited calculations including self- and cross-Kerr shifts, with the cubic correction retaining self-mode and two-mode virtual pro- cesses.

FIG. 4. Input-referred added-noise characterization. (a) Inverse SNR improvement, 1/R, versus inverse gain, 1/G, together with the fitted finite-gain noise model. (b) Pump-off and representative pump-on spectrum-analyzer traces for the same operating point. (c) Input- referred added-noise number versus signal frequency for the 7–3 and 8–2 signal–idler combinations. The dashed line denotes the phase- preserving quantum limit, Nadd = 1/2. Error bars propagate uncer- tainties from the fit, the Nrest calibration, and the pump-off reflection.
